title: Silver-bullet regression notes & ad-hoc rubric (evening scratchpad)
content:
Quick context / purpose:
- Evening scratchpad: trying to capture a small, repeatable ad-hoc rubric for fast triage of regressions when a new runtime patch or quantization profile lands.
- Primary aim: fast binary signal + lightweight severity bucket so I can route to SRE/infra or to model-onboarding team.
- This is intentionally informal — steps I followed, hypotheses, and minimal sample outputs.

How I ran the check (notes-to-self):
- Models compared: local/v1.4 (fp16 baseline) vs local/v1.5-q4_0 (new quant profile).
- Inference flags: temperature=0.0, max_tokens=120, stop=["\n\n"], stream=false.
- Workload: 120 random production prompts sampled from the daily sampler (lengths 40-380 tokens). I prioritized medium/long examples where we previously saw KV-cache interactions.
- Batch mode: continuous-batch enabled; batch size tuned to 8 for latency sim.
- Observed infra change: kernel patch (matmul reorder) + updated allocator in runtime 2025-02-12. Suspect falls back to slower path for some layer shapes.

Ad-hoc rubric (0-3, quick definitions):
- 0 = identical / no meaningful degradation (only noise-level diffs like punctuation).
- 1 = minor change (style shift, verbosity, harmless paraphrase). Not urgent.
- 2 = meaningful regression (missing facts, truncated content, repeated tokens, or changed intent). Requires developer review within 24–48h.
- 3 = severe regression (hallucination introducing wrong facts, contradictory instruction-following, or complete output collapse). Pager escalation.

Lightweight checklist per sample (tick/cross):
- [ ] Answer coherent? (yes/partial/no)
- [ ] Preserves requested instruction? (yes/partial/no)
- [ ] Logical contradictions? (no/yes)
- [ ] Unexpected token repetition? (no/yes)
- [ ] Latency spike >2x baseline? (no/yes)
- [ ] Deterministic mismatch for temp=0? (no/yes)

Representative sample snippets (kept short to reproduce quickly):
1) Prompt: "Summarize the following email thread and list three action items." (len ~ 220)
- v1.4: Clean 3-item bulleted list, each action tied to an actor.
- v1.5-q4_0: Item 2 missing actor; timeline shifted (says "by EOD Friday" where thread had "by next Tuesday").
- Score: 2 — wrong timeline, could break automation.
- Hypothesis: quantization changed numeric token decoding around dates; check numeric token mapping and softmax calibration.

2) Prompt: "Explain why HTTP 504 happens in plain terms for a novice." (len ~60)
- v1.4: Simple explanation with an analogy and 2 bullets for mitigation.
- v1.5-q4_0: Repeats same sentence twice, then ends abruptly (truncated).
- Score: 2 — repetition + truncation.
- Hypothesis: KV cache indexing off-by-one for certain sequence lengths leading to repeated attention chunk.

3) Prompt: "Convert the SQL to a parameterized prepared statement." (len ~80)
- v1.4: Correct transformation with placeholders and example binding.
- v1.5-q4_0: Introduces a syntactic error (missing comma in column list).
- Score: 3 — severe because it can introduce runtime failures if used.
- Hypothesis: tokenization boundary shift causing comma token mapped differently; verify tokenizer parity between profiles.

Observations across the 120 samples:
- Distribution of rubric scores: ~68% score 0/1, 24% score 2, 8% score 3 (high-level ballpark).
- Failure modes cluster around: numeric/date tokens, punctuation-heavy transforms (SQL/JSON), and longer contexts >250 tokens.
- Latency: median latency for v1.5-q4_0 ~1.1x baseline, but tail (95th) showed 2.8x for prompts with long prefix. That aligns with suspected kernel fallback.

Immediate actionable items (prioritized):
1) Repro script: create minimal reproducible cases for the top 6 score=3 samples. Assign to Ravi for quick repro job (include exact token offsets).
2) Tokenizer check: run parity check between v1.4 and v1.5-q4_0 for comma, period, numeric sequences and date-like tokens. (Maya)
3) Runtime trace: enable attention/key-cache debug logging for a failing long-case and capture layer-wise timings. (SRE/infra)
4) Rollback plan: hold rollout to a small canary and pin to v1.4 for critical routes until we isolate root cause. (Product + Release)

Notes / hypotheses to test (short list):
- Quantization mapping drift: new 4-bit packing may change seldom-used subtoken logits leading to a small set of tokens being over/under favored.
- Kernel shape fallback: certain sequence-layers hit a slow fallback that also interacts with batch re-ordering leading to timing-based nondeterminism.
- Post-processing bug: dedup/trimming step may interact differently because token IDs shifted; check trim heuristics (end-of-sequence detection).

Open questions (for follow-up):
- Is there telemetry capturing token-level divergence counts? If not, add a quick counter in the inference path (per-request top-1 token diff count).
- Are there model-specific softmax temperature knobs we can calibrate per-profile?
- Do we have a fast test harness to isolate tokenizer vs runtime? I should sketch one tomorrow.

Quick reproduction notes (how to give someone repro):
- Save prompt and model flags (temp=0, seed N/A). Run both binaries back-to-back on same machine, collect raw token ids from output, diff token sequences. If token ids match but text differs: postproc issue; if ids differ: tokenizer/runtime divergence.
- For truncation/repetition, also capture the last 64 tokens prior to failure — helps narrow the attention window.

To-do (short):
- [ ] Flesh out repro harness and upload minimal dataset to GH gist.
- [ ] Add counter in runtime for token-id mismatches across profiles.
- [ ] Run tokenizer parity across 5k common subtokens.
- [ ] Schedule 30m sync with infra + model-onboarding tomorrow morning.

Slack references I pinged while doing this (copied to keep context):
- #infra-kernel: thread 'matmul reorder regression?' at 2025-02-14 20:12
- #model-onboard: pinged Maya with example SQL failure 2025-02-15 09:05

Random jot: if numeric tokens are the culprit, maybe try a quick narrow quant retrain for the token id subset (targeted calibration) rather than full profile revert. Worth experimenting but needs low-risk gating.

End-of-scratchpad. Save this and create a short excerpt to paste into the JIRA ticket for a quick triage summary.
